newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT--Sallie Mae names 10-person slate.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT--Sallie Mae names 10-person slate.

text.p: Sallie Mae said Wednesday it would nominate 10 candidates to the holding company board as part of a privatization plan it would propose to shareholders. Sallie Mae proposed David Vitale as the company's chairman and said Lawrence Hough would remain the company's CEO until a successor could be found.
A full text of the company's press release follows.
Election To Board Of Proposed Holding Company; One-Third Of 15-Member Board Held Open For CRV
Business Editors

WASHINGTON, D.C.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--June 11, 1997-- FIRST CHICAGO VICE CHAIRMAN VITALE PROPOSED AS CHAIRMAN OF NEW BOARD AFTER TRANSITION TO PRIVATIZATION HOUGH TO RESIGN AS SALLIE MAE CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER

Sallie Mae (NYSE: SLM) announced today that it will nominate 10 candidates for election to the 15-member board of directors of the holding company as part of the privatization plan it will propose to shareholders. (See the attached list of Sallie Mae nominees.)

Upon receipt of a majority of the votes cast in the election of directors to the holding company board, the remaining 5 seats on the holding company board will be held for nominees submitted by the Committee to Restore Value (CRV). The CRV will also be proposing its own slate of director nominees. The CRV's 5-seat representation on the holding company's 15-seat board approximates the CRV's current 8-seat representation on Sallie Mae's existing 21-seat board.

In addition, the company has proposed David J. Vitale, Vice Chairman of First Chicago NBD Corporation, as non-executive Chairman of the holding company board. Mr. Vitale has served on the Sallie Mae board of directors for the last 20 years.

"Our conversations with shareholders and the outcome of recent votes on competing privatization plans demonstrate that while both sides have strong support among our shareholder base, neither has majority support," Vitale said. "As a result, we will amend our reorganization plan to provide for a new chief executive -- an individual with a substantial record of success outside of a GSE. We believe that Sallie Mae's owners want privatization, expansion of our proven business strategies, and CRV representation on, but not control of, the holding company board. Our revised slate provides this structure," added Vitale. New CEO To Be Selected

Following privatization, Sallie Mae's directors will be conducting a search for a new chief executive officer to head the company and review its management structure. Lawrence A. Hough, Sallie Mae's President and Chief Executive Officer, has agreed to remain in his position through the company's transition to a privatized company and until a successor has been named.

Hough said, "I intend to break the deadlock and free the new CEO to pursue continued growth in franchise and share value. We should not permit continued turmoil to undermine Sallie Mae's strength in the marketplace and support on Capitol Hill."

William Arceneaux, Chairman of the Sallie Mae (GSE) Board said, "For the last several years, Larry Hough has relentlessly pursued a privatization plan, overcoming skepticism and political barriers. This company can now enter an exciting new era as a direct result of Larry Hough's vision and leadership. We are prepared for the 21st century."

Mr. Hough has been President and Chief Executive Officer of Sallie Mae since 1990. Hough is responsible for introducing Sallie Mae's school-based strategy, which enabled the company to compete successfully with government direct lending. Under his leadership, Sallie Mae became the first government-sponsored enterprise (GSE) to secure privatization legislation from the U.S. Congress. These and other changes at Sallie Mae led to a tripling of the company's share price in less than two years to record price levels.

Earlier in his career, Hough launched the company's loan servicing operation, which contributes meaningfully to the strength of Sallie Mae's core business and offers great potential for further growth in income and share value. July Meeting Anticipated

As previously announced, Sallie Mae anticipates holding a special meeting of shareholders in July to consider and vote on a proposed plan of reorganization to privatize Sallie Mae and to choose between two slates of directors for election to the holding company board of directors -- the Sallie Mae slate described above or a slate of up to 15 nominees proposed by the CRV.

"Next month our shareholders will have the opportunity to support our proven business strategy with new leadership," Vitale concluded. "I am confident that our plan will be supported by our shareholders." Sallie Mae, a stockholder-owned corporation, is the nation's leading provider of financial services for postsecondary education needs. The corporation is the nation's largest source of funding and servicing support for education loans for students and their parents. The nominees for the proposed holding company board are:
